transport: Bluetooth LE to the Rolls LFP Connect app (Android/iOS) only. No RS-485. No Modbus. No documented CAN. G-Series metal-case 48 V golf and light-EV models have a CAN bus port, but its only documented use is driving the SOC indicator shipped with the battery; the manual's Appendix C gives the pinout of the INDICATOR's 11-pin Molex, not the frame format on the wire.
refutedOnReview: Refuted on two independent grounds.  GROUND 1 — the claim refutes itself. A dialect asserts "these models share one register map." The evidence explicitly concedes there is no map: "it is a shared ABSENCE of any published protocol, not a shared register map. There is no map to share." I confirmed this: grep for modbus\|rs485\|rs-485\|register over the full extracted text of docs/rolls-lfp-drop-in-manual-v4.pdf return
gotchas: Filed under no-comms because from Cabin Hub's side there is nothing to speak to, not because the battery is dumb. It has a BMS, a display and a phone app — but the BLE service, characteristics and payload format are unpublished, and a search for community reverse-engineering of the Rolls LFP Connect app turned up nothi
Do NOT guess that the BMS is a rebadged JBD/JK/Daly and reuse one of those BLE drivers. Nothing observed supports it and a wrong pack-level BMS decode is worse than no reading.

R-Series has no display and no reset button: it wakes only when a charger or load is attached. G-Series and S-Series have an onboard screen and a reset button. That difference matters for any bench session before it matters for a driver.
The 12 V/24 V generation documented in the 2021 manual (S-Series 12V & 24V LFP Operating Manual) describes no Bluetooth and no comms at all. If a cabin has an older Rolls drop-in, expect nothing.

S12-100LFP and a generic 'Rolls 12V 100Ah LiFePO4' are stocked at The Cabin Depot; R12-100LFP is on shop.rollsbattery.ca. This is the Rolls line most likely to actually turn up in a Quebec cabin, and it is the one with the least to talk to. checked: 2026-07-31
unmappedReports: BMS error codes ER0 Other/Unknown, ER1 Over Voltage, ER2 Under Voltage, ER3 Over Temperature, ER4 Under Temperature — no MetricKind carries a battery fault state, internal heater state (S-Series drop-ins are the self-heating ones; the onboard screen shows a Heating indicator), Bluetooth link status shown on the onboard display, per-cell voltages
